issue.title: complement
Can't pickle function delayed
issue.body:
I get a "_pickle.PicklingError: Can't pickle <function delayed at 0x7fceb5c89488>" when trying to use calculate on an instance method that returns a delayed. Afair this used to work until some days ago...

Minimal example:

```
from dask import delayed
from distributed import Client

class TestClass():
    def __init__(self):
        pass

    def do_something(self, value):
        return value + 10

    def get_delayed(self, value):
        return delayed(self.do_something)(value)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    c = Client('127.0.0.1:8786') # I have a scheduler and workers running locally

    tc = TestClass()

    print(c)

    d = tc.get_delayed(10)
    r = d.compute()

    print(r)
```

I'm using dask and distrubuted from git master:
In [3]: print(dask.__version__)

In [4]: print(distributed.__version__)

issue.title: Currying standard functions
issue.body:
I'd like to curry a large number of functions in `toolz/__init__.py`.  

This would allow us to use idioms like 

```
map(take(2), list_of_lists)
```

rather than

```
map(lambda L: take(2, L), list_of_lists)
```

In particular it would make thread_first and thread_last much more Pythonic

issue.title: Toolz.merge fails when provided one non-dict mapping
issue.body:
Here is a minimal reproducible example:

```python
In [1]: import toolz, collections

In [2]: class Foo(collections.Mapping):
   ...:     def __init__(self, d):
   ...:         self.d = d
   ...:     def __iter__(self):
   ...:         return iter(self.d)
   ...:     def __getitem__(self, key):
   ...:         return self.d[key]
   ...:     def __len__(self):
   ...:         return len(self.d)
   ...:

In [3]: d = Foo({1: 1})

In [4]: toolz.merge(d)
```
```python-traceback
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TypeError                                 Traceback (most recent call last)
<ipython-input-4-e5a2d80dd87f> in <module>
----> 1 toolz.merge(d)

~/miniconda/envs/dev/lib/python3.7/site-packages/toolz/dicttoolz.py in merge(*dicts, **kwargs)
     36     rv = factory()
     37     for d in dicts:
---> 38         rv.update(d)
     39     return rv
     40

TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable
```

I think that we might want to change the `dict` typecheck here to `Mapping`

issue.title: Is checks for `no_default` fail if string is pickled
issue.body:
Opening this for discussion, as the solution may be just "don't do that". Currently, many functions take an optional keyword argument with a default of `__no__default__`. This is checked for comparison with `is`, which in general is True if the strings are equal, and is quite fast. This fails however if the default argument is serialized using pickle:

``` python
In [1]: from pickle import dumps, loads

In [2]: s = '__no__default__'

In [3]: s is s
Out[3]: True

In [4]: s2 = loads(dumps(s))

In [5]: s is s2
Out[5]: False
```

This can cause problems in dask (or at least makes the graphs a bit more complicated), as we can't just transparently pass the string through as an argument. One solution might be to use `==` instead, although this incurs a minor speed penalty:

``` python
In [6]: %timeit s is s
10000000 loops, best of 3: 50.2 ns per loop

In [7]: %timeit s == s
10000000 loops, best of 3: 57.5 ns per loop

In [8]: %timeit s == s2
10000000 loops, best of 3: 59 ns per loop
```

These numbers are slightly different for python 3:

``` python
In [6]: %timeit s is s
10000000 loops, best of 3: 45.2 ns per loop

In [7]: %timeit s == s
10000000 loops, best of 3: 52.9 ns per loop

In [8]: %timeit s == s2
10000000 loops, best of 3: 62.2 ns per loop
```
